news.headline: Was CrowdStrike’s $43.9 Billion Bid for Zscaler the Right Move at the Wrong Time?
news.summary: CrowdStrike just posted its best quarter ever, then paid a fortune in stock for a rival whose own guidance vanished. Investors now face a year of waiting to learn whether strength or ambition sets the price.

news.headline: Own Palo Alto Stock? Watch Its Deferred Revenue
news.summary: Palo Alto Networks closed at $356.14 on Wednesday, Nov 25, up 0.9%. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF fell 0.3% the same day. On Nov 18, after the market closed, the company reported results. It also said it plans to buy Applied Compute for $4.5 billion, paid in stock. The stock jumped 6.4% the next day. This article looks past the price, at the company's own cash and contracts.

news.headline: Truist Sees 52% Upside in Zscaler, and the Reason Has Nothing to Do With Zscaler’s Valuation
news.summary: Key TakeawaysTruist kept its Buy rating on Zscaler and raised its price target to $340 from $250, 52% above Wednesday’s close. The $340 matches Truist’s $300 CrowdStrike target times 1.

news.headline: Bridgewater Sees 1-in-3 Odds of a Destabilizing Cyberattack. CrowdStrike’s Workload Is Already “Up 50%”
news.summary: Key TakeawaysBridgewater is managing money on a one-in-three chance of an economically destabilizing cyberattack within a year, and incident-response firms are reportedly out of capacity. CrowdStrike’s record $419 million of net new ARR, up 58%, shows the attack surge turning into subscription revenue.
